newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No damaging cold forecast for Brazil coffee -Somar.
newsitem.headline: No damaging cold forecast for Brazil coffee -Somar.

text.p: There is no frost threat for Brazil's key coffee regions in the coming six to eight days, independent meteorologist Somar said.
Rainy and cloudy weather should continue today in the south of Minas and north Sao Paulo but sunshine should return from Friday, Somar said in a regular weather update.
Minimum temperatures should remain between 12 and 15 degrees Celsius in Parana and the southwest region.

From the night of May 19, a new cold front should arrive in the south of the country but for the time being weather models do not show the entry of any polar air mass which could lead to critical temperatures in the coffee regions.
The world's coffee market has already started to look towards the Brazilian winter which brings the threat of frosts.

According to some records, the earliest frost in the last 100 years to hit the coffee regions was on May 31 but the most critical months are June and July. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
